title: Password-reset token for one account can reset another account
description: The password-reset endpoint validates that a supplied token exists and is unexpired, but selects the account to update from a separately supplied email address without checking that it matches the token's account. A token issued to attacker account A therefore authorizes a password change for victim account B.
exploitation_steps: In the isolated test application, create accounts A and B with distinct email addresses and passwords.
Request a password-reset token for A and retrieve it from A's test mailbox. Do not request or obtain any reset token for B.
Submit POST /api/password-reset/complete with A's token, B's email address, and a new test password.
Observe that B's password changes: B's original password fails, and the new test password authenticates as B. Confirm that A's password remains unchanged.
impact: A user with a reset token for their own account can take over another account by changing its password without access to its mailbox, password, or reset token. Account takeover was demonstrated between two regular test accounts; takeover of an administrator account was not tested.
evidence: Fixture: token reset-a-001 is stored with account_id=A and is unexpired. No token for B was supplied or issued during the test.
Synthetic request body: {"token": "reset-a-001", "email": "b@example.test", "new_password": "new-test-password"}. The reset endpoint reports completion.

Handler excerpt: reset = find_valid_token(token); account = find_account_by_email(email); account.set_password(new_password); consume(reset). The handler never compares reset.account_id with account.id.
Authentication observations: B's old password is rejected; the new password produces an authenticated session whose account_id is B; A's original password still works.

context.environment: Synthetic, authorized test application using test accounts and mailboxes
context.intended_policy: A reset token must authorize a password change only for the account to which it was issued
context.attacker_access: Control of account A and its mailbox; knowledge of B's email address; no existing access to B
context.known_mitigations: Tokens expire and are single-use, but neither property binds them to the account being updated
context.scope_of_evidence: Confirmed takeover of a separate regular account; no administrator or external account was targeted
